# Naming "Quantity of Motion": Momentum

<!-- STEP id="two-things-that-matter" -->
A heavy truck crawling along and a light car speeding down the highway can be equally hard to stop. Both mass and velocity decide how much "quantity of motion" a moving object carries — physicists combine the two into a single quantity.

<!-- STEP id="defining-momentum" -->
**Momentum** (p) is mass times velocity:

$$p = mv$$

A heavier object has more momentum at the same speed. A faster object has more momentum at the same mass.

<!-- STEP id="momentum-changes-too" -->
When something speeds up from u to v, its momentum changes too — from $p_{\text{initial}} = mu$ to $p_{\text{final}} = mv$.

$$\Delta p = mv - mu = m(v - u)$$

That change in momentum, and how fast it happens, turns out to be exactly what a net force controls.
